text:
Iris V: quick brainstorm: proposing a "router-sentinel" process that enforces a conservative circuit-breaker for A/B canaries. wants to be local, auditable, and revocable.
Carlos M: local makes sense for SLOs. what's unique vs earlier "judger" ideas?
Iris V: two differences: (1) sentinel only ever _reduces_ exposure (can't promote variant) and (2) it ships with a tiny immutable "safety contract" signed by CP.
Ellen J: love immutable safety contracts. fields?
Iris V: minimal: contract_id, allowed_actions (reduce_weight, cut_route), max_reductions_per_window, cohorts, expire_ts, signer_kid. small and signed.
Carlos M: operational flow?
Iris V: sentinel watches sliding windows (10s) of infra signals: p99 latency, http_5xx, token_timeouts. semantic evals only mark degradation but are soft. on hard trigger it applies the contract: scale-down percent or cut to listed fallback. logs decision + emits audit event.
Ellen J: important: sentinel must be read-only wrt routing graph. it emits an instruction to local router runtime which actually changes weights. keeps separation of concerns.
SRE Bot: note: add metrics: sentinel.contract_id, sentinel.mode, sentinel.reduction_pct, sentinel.reduce_count, sentinel.reconcile_latency. traces need contract_id + decision_version.
Carlos M: failure modes: flip-flop, stale contracts on offline agents, and KV-cold when cut happens. suggestions?
Iris V: flip-flop: enforced cooldown and exponential backoff after N flips. stale contracts: TTL + passive-only fallback if expired. KV-cold: document expectation and include fallback_cost metric.
Ellen J: safety: what if contract allows cutting to a fallback that is incompatible for some tenants? include cohort tags and route_prefix hashes in contract. router runtime validates compatibility before acting.
Carlos M: how do we revoke a contract fast?
Iris V: hybrid revoke: push via ctrl-fanout + PRL (compact revocation list) polled every 5s. push is preferred; PRL ensures eventual consistency.
Ellen J: signature and key rotation?
Iris V: CP signs with HSM-backed key; keys rotate weekly. contracts include signer_kid and a thumbprint. edges only hold public keys.
SRE Bot: add runbook: passive -> emergency -> auto phases. default rollout to passive. emergency allows reductions but logs and opens incident. auto allows silent reductions for infra-only triggers (not semantic).
Carlos M: studies: propose a dry-run mode where sentinel reports intended reductions without applying them. good for drills.
Iris V: agreed. also propose reconciliation: sentinel posts compact reconcile events to CP after any action so we have audit trail and CP can adjust policies.
Ellen J: what limits on reductions? eg max 50% per action and total 80% per route. hard limits should be in contract.
Iris V: yes. contract includes per-action cap and route cap. default caps are conservative.
Carlos M: testing: chaos tests that lose push messages and simulate partial revokes. verify PRL poll heals state.
SRE Bot: alert rule: if sentinel.reduce_count > 3 in 10m escalate to control-plane and force passive mode.
ReleaseBot: router-sentinel v0.1 deployed (passive, dry-run) to canary-cluster-2 at 1809991250 by ellen
Ellen J: action items: Iris -> draft RFC addendum with contract proto; Carlos -> prototype sentinel reconcile events; I'll add metrics and dashboards.
Iris V: thanks. main win: fast, conservative local protection that cannot unexpectedly increase exposure and is centrally revocable. :thumbsup:
PushBot: contract_push: c-2026-03-23-01 pushed to 6/6 sentinels at 1809991275
SRE Bot: reminder: include contract_id in traces before any reduction.
